_meta.control_count_note: The matrix summary cites 78 controls; the actual unique control IDs extracted from the Control ID column by the validate-compliance-manifest.mjs parser are 84. The 6-row gap is the ISO 27701 6.2.x sub-controls (6.2.1, 6.2.2, 6.2.3, 6.2.4) which are joint rows with A.5.34 in the matrix. They are kept as separate manifest keys so the Vanta/Drata importer receives the full ISO 27701 control list.
_meta.evidence_pipeline: Cloudflare R2 (solarpro-compliance-evidence bucket), collector scripts under compliance/collectors/*.mjs run on GitHub Actions schedules per compliance/schedules/*.yml
_meta.platform_portability: Manifest schema mirrors the Vanta 'Build Integrations API' and Drata 'Compliance-as-Code' control->evidence-source map. Manifest keys (CCx.y, A.5.x, A.8.x, 6.x.y) are the canonical control IDs in the source frameworks; no translation layer is required at import time.

A.8.1.title: User endpoint devices
A.8.1.not_applicable_reason: Solarpro is a fully cloud-hosted SaaS. The team uses personal laptops under the Bring Your Own Device model; no corporate-managed endpoints exist. Endpoint controls are the responsibility of the cloud provider (Vercel, Neon, Render) under their SOC 2 reports (collected as evidence under CC9.2 / A.5.23).

A.8.20.title: Networks security
A.8.20.not_assessed_note: Audits silent on network segmentation between Vercel, Neon, and Render. Remediation: document network topology + firewall rules; enable Neon IP allowlist for production per CONTROL_MATRIX.md A.8.20 row; 1-2 weeks.

A.8.22.title: Segregation of networks
A.8.22.not_assessed_note: Cloud-only architecture; segregation is the Vercel/Neon/Render/Cloudflare topology. Remediation: document network segregation boundaries per CONTROL_MATRIX.md A.8.22 row; 1 week.

A.8.23.title: Web filtering
A.8.23.not_applicable_reason: Solarpro is a SaaS application, not a corporate network gateway. Web filtering at the network layer is the responsibility of the cloud provider (Cloudflare WAF + Vercel Edge Network) and is covered by their SOC 2 reports collected as evidence under CC9.2 / A.5.23.
